subject: Packaging decision: seat vs throughput and feature bundling for StackCare
messages:
From: Rajiv Shah <rajiv@stackcare.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Lopez <monica@stackcare.io>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Packaging options — our usage profile attached

Hi Ben / Kimberly,

Thanks again for walking through Redwood last week. Attaching our Q3 usage export — we wanted to get your recommendation on the packaging direction. High level:

- Current profile: bursty inference (morning and late-evening peaks), 60% chat/assist, 40% batch embeddings.
- Monthly token baseline ~1.1B but spikes to 2.8B in weeks with product events.

Questions we care about:
1) For this profile, is Dedicated-Elastic or Compact (throughput-oriented) the better fit for cost vs latency?
2) If we pick a compact seat-based plan, how does bursting work — can we attach temporary throughput credits or a burst pool?
3) Which feature bundles (logging retention, KV cache lift, higher concurrency) are recommended for our customer-facing workflows?

We're also trying to understand commercial levers — onboarding credits, first-year discounts, and whether we can get a phased rollout (start with pilot throughput, then scale).

Attachment: stackcare_usage_report_Q3.csv

Would appreciate a concise recommendation and a proposed next step (workshop or quote).

Thanks,
Rajiv Shah
Head of ML Platform | StackCare

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Shah <rajiv@stackcare.io>, Monica Lopez <monica@stackcare.io>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Packaging options — our usage profile attached

Rajiv — thanks for the export, that helps a lot. TL;DR: for StackCare's mix I'd recommend a two-phase approach. Details and immediate asks below.

Recommendation (short):
- Phase 1 (pilot, 2 months): Dedicated-Elastic with a small committed seat pool sized to baseline (~1.2B tokens/month) + a 20% burst buffer. This keeps latency predictable for chat while capping committed spend.
- Phase 2 (scale): Move to a mixed model (reserved capacity for low-latency routes + hosted metered for batch jobs). This reduces unit cost for embeddings while preserving chat SLOs.

Why: your spikes drive up token cost if run pure metered; dedicated capacity with burstable overlay lets you keep tail-latency in check and use metered for the heavy nightly embedding runs.

Feature bundling notes (recommendations):
- KV cache (business): enable for chat routes — saves ~25% tokens on repeated context.
- Extended logs (30d): recommended only for a short audit window; can be tiered to reduce retention cost.
- Concurrency boost (feature pack B): add for peak hours; we can gate it with an autoscale policy.

Commercial / next steps:
- I'll put together a short matrix (attached) that maps baseline vs burst sizing.
- Proposed next step: 60-minute workshop with Product + Infra to model cost curves; can we do early next week?
- If you confirm a 12-month pilot commit we can discuss an onboarding credit.

Attachment: redwood_pack_matrix_v3.pdf

Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Shah <rajiv@stackcare.io>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 10:25:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Packaging options — our usage profile attached

Rajiv / Ben — quick pricing and concession note from my side so we have clarity going into the workshop: 

Commercial options we can offer (StackCare):
- Option A (Committed throughput): 12-month committed capacity at baseline (1.2B tokens/mo) + 20% burst window. Pricing: 10% discount vs list for the committed portion.
- Option B (Seat + Metered): Moderate seat commitment for low-latency routes + metered for batch — includes a 7% blended discount on committed spend.

One-time incentives:
- Onboarding credit: USD 15k credit applied within first 60 days if you sign a 12-month MSA.
- Pilot uplift: For a 3-month pilot we can provide 30% off pilot overage rate for the first pilot period to limit tail-cost risk.

Operational guardrails:
- We can configure a burst pool (pre-funded credits) that auto-applies when dedicated capacity is saturated; credits are consumed before metered billing kicks in.
- Can add an automatic rollback policy to fall back to metered with rate limiting if latency SLOs are at risk.

If you want, I can draft a short term-sheet summarizing Option A vs B plus the credit language (deal id: DC-20261121-STACK-01). Ben — can you confirm if we should model both 6- and 12-month commitments in the workshop?

Kimberly Park
Director, Sales Ops | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

From: Rajiv Shah <rajiv@stackcare.io>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Monica Lopez <monica@stackcare.io>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Packaging options — our usage profile attached

Ben / Kimberly — this is helpful, thank you. Summary and next steps from our side:

- We like Phase 1 as Dedicated-Elastic + 20% burst buffer. We are comfortable with a 12-month pilot/commit.
- Please model Option A (12-month commit) and Option B (seat+metered) with blended unit economics for our peak weeks vs baseline weeks.
- Confirm onboarding credit and pilot uplift language in the term-sheet.
- Next step: schedule the workshop — mornings next Tue/Wed (PST) work for our infra/product leads.

Quote:

Can you send an updated quote + a draft term-sheet (PDF) and a DocuSign link when available? We'll loop in procurement after the workshop.

Thanks — looking forward to the workshop.
Rajiv
Head of ML Platform | StackCare
